d1.t: The court records this without judgement. Mostly.

d14.t: An adult has not been located.

d17.t: Someone pour the evidence another drink.

e.assassin.hit.1.t: It was Merlin! The Assassin strikes true! Evil steals the victory!

e.assassin.hit.2.t: Merlin falls! All those clever hints, and look where it got them.

e.assassin.hit.3.t: Bullseye! Merlin is found, and evil wins it all!

e.assassin.miss.1.t: Not Merlin! The Assassin missed! Good triumphs!

e.assassin.miss.2.t: Wrong target! Merlin lives, and Camelot is saved!

e.assassin.miss.3.t: The blade misses! Merlin survives! What a performance.

e.assassin.slow.1.t: The Assassin is taking their time. Somewhere, Merlin is sweating.

e.assassin.slow.2.t: Still choosing. Every good player is aging visibly.

e.assassin.slow.3.t: Take your time, Assassin. We'll all just hold our breath.

e.assassin.start.1.t: Three quests succeed! But wait. The Assassin may yet strike. Find Merlin, and evil steals the game.

e.assassin.start.2.t: Good has won the quests. Now the Assassin chooses one target. Guess Merlin, and it's all for nothing.

e.assassin.start.3.t: Not so fast, heroes! The Assassin emerges from the shadows. Merlin, try to look ordinary.

e.assassin.strike.1.t: The Assassin has chosen. Let's see if the blade finds its mark.

e.assassin.strike.2.t: The dagger falls. Was it Merlin?

e.assassin.strike.3.t: A target is chosen. The moment of truth.

e.award.assassin.1.t: And finally, the Assassin, who found Merlin. Terrifyingly good at their job.

e.award.assassin.2.t: A special dishonour for the Assassin, whose aim was perfect. Remind me never to annoy you.

e.award.homebody.1.t: The Homebody Award, for going on the fewest quests. Sat by the fire. Very cosy.

e.award.homebody.2.t: Least Invited Knight. They'll tell you it was strategy.

e.award.kingmaker.1.t: The Kingmaker Award, for leading quests to success. Arthur would be proud.

e.award.kingmaker.2.t: Best Leader. Picked a winning team, which is more than most can say.

e.award.merlin.1.t: And finally, Merlin. Who survived. Hiding in plain sight, like a wizard should.

e.award.merlin.2.t: A special honour for Merlin, who survived the assassin. Clever, clever wizard.

e.award.poker_face.1.t: Best Poker Face, for being evil and going on successful quests anyway. Chillingly patient.

e.award.poker_face.2.t: The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing Award. Evil, trusted, and smiling the entire time.

e.award.saboteur.1.t: Master Saboteur, for sneaking onto failed quests. Absolutely shameless. We salute you.

e.award.saboteur.2.t: The Butterfingers Award, for being on the quests that mysteriously failed.

e.award.skeptic.1.t: The Drawbridge Award, for rejecting almost everything. Nobody gets in. Nobody.

e.award.skeptic.2.t: Chief Skeptic of Camelot. Trusted no one, and was right at least once.

e.award.traveller.1.t: Most Well-Travelled, for going on the most quests. Frequent rider miles: enormous.

e.award.traveller.2.t: The Wandering Knight Award. Never met a quest they didn't join.

e.award.trusting.1.t: The Golden Retriever Award, for approving nearly everything. Bless your trusting heart.

e.award.trusting.2.t: Most Trusting Knight. Never met a team they didn't like.

e.award.unlucky_leader.1.t: The Rejected Royalty Award, for having their proposals turned down the most. Heavy is the head.

e.award.unlucky_leader.2.t: Least Popular Leader. The crown kept slipping off.

e.awards.intro.1.t: And now, the Royal Honours! Awards nobody asked for, presented with great ceremony.

e.awards.intro.2.t: Before we go, the Court presents its honours. Some are compliments. Most are not.

e.awards.intro.3.t: It's time for the awards! Please hold your applause, and your grudges, until the end.

e.awards.outro.1.t: Congratulations to all, and especially to the liars. Rematch?

e.awards.outro.2.t: That concludes the ceremony. Your grudges may now be carried into the rematch.

e.awards.outro.3.t: Thank you, thank you. Same time next game? Same betrayals?

e.discussion.final10.1.t: Ten seconds! Wrap up your wild theories.

e.discussion.final10.2.t: Ten seconds left. Last chance to accuse someone without evidence.

e.discussion.final10.3.t: Ten seconds! Speak now, or forever hold your suspicion.

e.discussion.over.1.t: Time! Put the pitchforks down. Gently.

e.discussion.over.2.t: That's enough talk. To the decision!

e.discussion.over.3.t: And the debate is over. Nobody was convinced. Excellent.

e.discussion.start.2.t: The floor is open. Make your case, and make it loud.

e.discussion.start.3.t: Talk amongst yourselves. Preferably about each other.

e.end.evil_assassin.1.t: Evil wins by assassination! Good did all that work for nothing. Delicious.

e.end.evil_assassin.2.t: Merlin is gone, and evil takes the crown. What a twist!

e.end.evil_missions.1.t: Three quests failed. Evil wins! Mordred sends his regards.

e.end.evil_missions.2.t: Evil triumphs! Camelot falls, one sabotaged quest at a time.

e.end.evil_rejections.1.t: Five rejected parties! The kingdom collapses in bureaucracy. Evil wins!

e.end.evil_rejections.2.t: Nobody could agree on anything, so evil wins. Classic committee.

e.end.good.1.t: Good wins! Camelot is saved! Please, try to be humble about it.

e.end.good.2.t: Victory for the loyal servants of Arthur! The realm endures!

e.end.roles.1.t: Now, let's unmask everyone. Prepare to feel betrayed.

e.end.roles.2.t: Time for the big reveal. Who was who? Brace yourselves.

e.leader.new.1.t: The crown passes on. Try to do better than the last one.

e.leader.new.2.t: A new leader takes the throne. It's warm. Don't ask why.

e.leader.new.4.t: The crown moves along, like a hot potato with a coat of arms.

e.lobby.all_ready.1.t: Everyone is ready. Host, the kingdom awaits your finger.

e.lobby.all_ready.2.t: All hands raised! Well, all phones. Start the game, my liege.

e.lobby.all_ready.3.t: The whole table is ready. Rarely have so many been so wrong about being ready.

e.lobby.enough.1.t: Six players! We have enough for a proper conspiracy.

e.lobby.enough.2.t: That's a full fellowship. The treachery may now commence whenever the host is ready.

e.lobby.enough.3.t: Enough knights at last. Somebody press start before anyone gets cold feet.

e.lobby.idle.1.t: Still waiting. The candles are getting shorter, and so is my patience.

e.lobby.idle.2.t: Take your time. Camelot has only been under threat for several centuries.

e.lobby.idle.3.t: Is anyone going to start this, or shall we simply gaze at one another all night?

e.lobby.join.10.t: And in walks trouble. Lovely to have you.

e.lobby.join.2.t: Ooh, a new arrival. They look innocent. That's always a bad sign.

e.lobby.join.4.t: A fresh face! Let's see how long it stays fresh.

e.lobby.join.5.t: Someone new has joined. Hide the silverware.

e.lobby.join.6.t: Another knight arrives, armed with a phone and questionable judgement.

e.lobby.join.7.t: Hark! A newcomer! Everyone pretend you're nice.

e.lobby.join.8.t: Welcome to Camelot. Please mind the daggers.

e.lobby.welcome.1.t: Welcome, welcome, to the Round Table! Scan the code, pick a name, and try to look trustworthy.

e.lobby.welcome.2.t: Ah, guests! Do come in. Phones out, room code in, and leave your honesty at the door.

e.lobby.welcome.3.t: Gather round, lords and ladies. Tonight, someone at this table will lie to your face. Splendid!

e.lobby.welcome.4.t: The hall is open! Join on your phones. The betrayal is free, and so are the snacks, presumably.

e.mission.1.1.t: Mission one! A gentle start. Nobody has any evidence, which has never stopped anyone.

e.mission.1.2.t: The first quest. A blank slate. Let's see who scribbles on it first.

e.mission.2.1.t: Mission two. The plot thickens like week-old porridge.

e.mission.2.2.t: On to the second quest. Grudges are now fully loaded.

e.mission.3.1.t: Mission three. The middle of the story, where everyone starts lying more confidently.

e.mission.3.2.t: The third quest. Half the realm hangs in the balance. No pressure.

e.mission.4.1.t: Mission four. With a big table, evil needs two fails here. Do the maths, then distrust the mathematicians.

e.mission.4.2.t: The fourth quest. Things are getting dramatic. I've ordered extra candles.

e.mission.5.1.t: Mission five. The final quest. Everything comes down to this. Please, nobody faint.

e.mission.5.2.t: The last quest! All of Camelot is watching. Mostly through its fingers.

e.night.complete.1.t: Dawn breaks. Everyone knows exactly what they know. Act accordingly.

e.night.complete.2.t: The sun rises, and so does suspicion. Let us begin.

e.night.complete.3.t: Morning, everyone. Evil had a lovely night, I'm told.

e.night.intro.1.t: Night falls over Camelot. Read your secrets in silence. No gasping. No winking. I'm looking at you.

e.night.intro.2.t: The night reveals its secrets. Study your phone, memorise what you see, and act natural. Naturally.

e.night.intro.3.t: Darkness settles over the castle. The wicked know each other now. The good know... very little. As usual.

e.proposal.forced.1.t: Fifth proposal! No vote this time. Whatever the leader picks, rides. Democracy has left the building.

e.proposal.forced.2.t: Four rejections. This leader's party goes, no questions asked. Choose very, very carefully.

e.proposal.locked.1.t: The party is chosen! Now we vote.

e.proposal.locked.2.t: The leader has spoken. Let the court decide.

e.proposal.locked.3.t: A fellowship is proposed. Prepare your opinions.

e.proposal.slow.1.t: Any time now, leader. The quest isn't getting any younger.

e.proposal.slow.2.t: Still choosing? Even Merlin is getting bored.

e.proposal.slow.3.t: The leader deliberates. The rest of us age gracefully.

e.proposal.start.1.t: The leader must now choose a party. Choose wisely, or at least choose quickly.

e.proposal.start.2.t: Time to pick a team. Leader, everyone is judging your every tap.

e.proposal.start.3.t: Assemble your fellowship, my liege. The table is watching your thumbs.

e.proposal.start.4.t: Pick your companions. Remember, friendship is temporary. Voting records are forever.

e.quest.begins.1.t: The quest begins! Party members, choose your card. Success, or... something else.

e.quest.begins.2.t: Into the wilderness they go. Quest members, play your cards on your phones.

e.quest.begins.3.t: The fellowship departs. Good may only succeed. Evil may do as it pleases. Choose.

e.quest.begins.4.t: Off on the quest! Everyone else, look anywhere except at their faces. Actually no, look right at them.

e.quest.close_call.1.t: One fail, but quest four needs two. The quest survives. Barely.

e.quest.close_call.2.t: A traitor struck, but not hard enough. The quest succeeds on a technicality.

e.quest.fail_many.1.t: Multiple fails! The traitors aren't even trying to hide now.

e.quest.fail_many.2.t: More than one fail! Evil brought friends to this quest.

e.quest.fail_many.3.t: Several betrayals! That wasn't sabotage, that was a team-building exercise.

e.quest.fail_one.1.t: One fail. Just one. A single, solitary traitor. How intimate.

e.quest.fail_one.2.t: Failed! Someone on that quest is not who they say they are.

e.quest.fail_one.3.t: One betrayal, and the quest falls. Look around. One of them did it.

e.quest.reveal.1.t: Drumroll, please. Let's reveal the cards. One. By. One.

e.quest.reveal.2.t: The moment of truth. Let's open the cards.

e.quest.reveal.3.t: Now, let's see what our brave adventurers really did.

e.quest.sealed.1.t: All the cards are in. Let's shuffle these, shall we?

e.quest.sealed.2.t: Every card is sealed. The truth is in the deck.

e.quest.sealed.3.t: The cards are played. No take-backsies.

e.quest.success.1.t: Success! The quest triumphs! Everyone act surprised.

e.quest.success.2.t: Victory! The quest succeeds! Evil is either sleeping, or scheming.

e.quest.success.3.t: A successful quest! Good gains ground. For now.

e.quest.success.4.t: Clean as a whistle! The quest is a success.

e.rejection.3.1.t: Three rejections. Two more failed votes would be... a problem. Just saying.

e.rejection.3.2.t: That's three rejected parties. The kingdom grows restless.

e.rejection.4.1.t: Four rejections! The next leader's party goes without a vote. Everyone, panic quietly.

e.rejection.4.2.t: Four in a row. The next proposal is binding. Choose like your crown depends on it.

e.rematch.instant.1.t: Everyone wants a rematch already! Healing is overrated.

e.rematch.instant.2.t: A unanimous rematch! Nobody learned a thing. Wonderful.

e.rematch.lobby.1.t: Back to the hall! Shall we betray each other again?

e.rematch.lobby.2.t: Round two! New roles, same old friends, fresh new lies.

e.rematch.lobby.3.t: Welcome back to the lobby. Your reputations, sadly, came with you.

e.score.decider.1.t: Two all! It comes down to the final quest!

e.score.decider.2.t: Level at two apiece. The next quest decides the fate of Camelot!

e.score.evil_two.1.t: Two failures! One more and evil takes the realm.

e.score.evil_two.2.t: Evil leads two to nothing. Good, this is what we call a crisis.

e.score.good_two.1.t: Two quests to good. One more and Camelot is saved. Probably.

e.score.good_two.2.t: Good leads two to nothing. Evil, it's time to get creative.

e.start.opening.1.t: Hear ye, hear ye! The game begins. Check your phones, guard your faces, and trust... absolutely no one.

e.start.opening.2.t: Let the treachery commence! Your roles await. Do try not to gasp out loud.

e.start.opening.3.t: And so it begins. Loyal servants of Arthur, minions of Mordred. Look at your phones, and keep your poker face.

e.start.opening.4.t: The gates of Camelot close behind you. Somewhere among you, evil grins politely. Look at your roles.

e.vote.approved.1.t: Approved! The quest party rides forth!

e.vote.approved.2.t: The court agrees! Remarkable. Let's see if it regrets it.

e.vote.approved.3.t: The fellowship is approved. Pack light. Trust lighter.

e.vote.approved.4.t: Approved. Off they go, into danger, and possibly into betrayal.

e.vote.rejected.1.t: Rejected! Back to the drawing board.

e.vote.rejected.2.t: The court says no. The crown moves on.

e.vote.rejected.3.t: Denied! That party will not be riding anywhere.

e.vote.rejected.4.t: Rejected. Somewhere, a leader quietly sulks.

e.vote.reveal.1.t: The votes are in. Let's see who trusts whom.

e.vote.reveal.2.t: And now, the moment of truth. Or at least, the moment of votes.

e.vote.reveal.3.t: Reveal the ballots! Let the judging begin.

e.vote.start.1.t: Approve or reject? Vote on your phones. Secretly. Then reveal everything publicly. Fun!

e.vote.start.2.t: Cast your votes! Every one of them will be shown to everyone. No pressure.

e.vote.start.3.t: To the ballot! Remember, your vote is secret for about ten seconds.

e.vote.start.4.t: Vote now. History is watching, and history is a terrible gossip.

e.vote.stragglers.1.t: Some of you are still voting. It's a yes or a no, not a sonnet.

e.vote.stragglers.2.t: We're waiting on a few stragglers. Take your time. We'll just stare at you.

e.vote.stragglers.3.t: Still deciding? Fascinating. Truly. Do go on.

e.vote.stragglers.4.t: A few votes remain. The suspense is unbearable. Mostly for me.

e.vote.tie.1.t: A tie! And a tie means rejection. Arithmetic is cruel.

e.vote.tie.2.t: Dead even, which means the party is rejected. Blame mathematics.

e.vote.unanimous_no.1.t: Unanimous rejection! Nobody liked that. Not even the leader, apparently.

e.vote.unanimous_no.2.t: Every vote says no. Ouch. That's going in the history books.

e.vote.unanimous_yes.1.t: Unanimous approval! Either everyone trusts this team, or someone is a very good liar.

e.vote.unanimous_yes.2.t: Every single vote says yes. That's either beautiful or deeply suspicious.

n1.t: Fresh game, fresh loyalties, same suspicious eye contact.

n10.t: Submitted at the bell. Confidence, with the paperwork of panic.

n11.t: The leader selected themselves. A touching vote of self-interest.

n12.t: The leader stayed home. Either humility, or an alibi with excellent tailoring.

n13.t: The identical party returns, now with absolutely no new information.

n14.t: You rejected this party before. Nostalgia truly is incurable.

n15.t: That failed fellowship has been reheated, and plated as strategy.

n16.t: The successful band is back together. The ego tour begins now.

n17.t: Someone has a third consecutive quest. Frequent-flyer treason points unlocked.

n18.t: Mission three, and someone still has cleaner boots than everyone else.

n19.t: One member changed. Behold, radical reform.

n2.t: A rematch. Because apparently, the previous betrayal lacked closure.

n20.t: The rejected leader returns, carrying no resentment whatsoever.

n21.t: Unanimous approval. The rare sound of everyone being wrong together.

n22.t: Unanimous rejection. The table has discovered teamwork, through spite.

n23.t: A tie rejects the party. Even arithmetic has trust issues here.

n23f1.t: No, staring at the dissenters will not change the count.

n23f2.t: The motion fails. The grudges, however, pass unanimously.

n23f3.t: Please direct complaints to mathematics, who will ignore them.

n23f4.t: A dead heat is still dead. Lovely symmetry, though.

n24.t: Approved by one vote. A mandate written in disappearing ink.

n25.t: Rejected by one vote. Someone just became tonight's group-chat topic.

n26.t: One lone reject, bravely ruining the family photo.

n27.t: One lone approve. Hope is adorable when isolated.

n28.t: Someone rejected a party containing themselves. Self-awareness, or insurance fraud?

n29.t: Every proposed member approved. The product endorsed itself.

n3.t: A new leader holds the crown. Try not to make it look like evidence.

n30.t: Several party members rejected their own trip. Read the reviews.

n31.t: Same party, different vote. Character development, or weather vane?

n32.t: Someone keeps approving. A golden retriever has entered parliament.

n33.t: Someone keeps rejecting. The drawbridge has a drawbridge.

n34.t: Two rejected parties. Mild dysfunction has become a theme.

n35.t: Three rejections. The round table is now mostly sharp corners.

n36.t: Four rejections. The next leader gets consent removed from the menu.

n36f1.t: One more rejection, and democracy is taken behind the castle.

n36f2.t: The fifth leader is warming up their benevolent dictatorship.

n36f3.t: Do reject again. I enjoy watching consequences put on boots.

n36f4.t: Next proposal comes with no ballot, and several raised eyebrows.

n37.t: Fifth proposal. Binding, vote-free, and sponsored by consequences.

n37f1.t: You had four chances to cooperate. The rulebook has stopped asking.

n37f2.t: The table wanted certainty. It has received compulsory tourism.

n37f3.t: No vote this time. Your previous votes were quite sufficient.

n37f4.t: Consent has left a note, and gone to the tavern.

n38.t: First proposal approved. Suspiciously efficient. Check everyone for wires.

n39.t: After all those rejections, a quest finally escaped committee.

n4.t: This discussion is so quiet, I can hear the alibis fermenting.

n40.t: Zero fails. Either heroes, cowards, or excellent accountants.

n41.t: Exactly one fail. A solo artist has entered the charts.

n42.t: Multiple fails. Treason has formed a project team.

n42f1.t: At least the traitors found colleagues, in this economy.

n42f2.t: That was less sabotage than a departmental initiative.

n42f3.t: One fail whispers. Several fails submit a quarterly report.

n42f4.t: The conspiracy has apparently secured group health insurance.

n43.t: Quest four survived one fail, because the large-table rules enjoy chaos.

n43f1.t: One saboteur did the work, and still failed the assignment.

n43f2.t: Somewhere, evil is rereading the two-fail footnote, very slowly.

n43f3.t: A technical success. The most irritating species of success.

n43f4.t: The second fail was invited. It declined to attend.

n44.t: Narrowly approved, successfully completed. Democracy accidentally shipped a feature.

n45.t: Unanimously approved, then failed. Put that confidence in a museum.

n45f1.t: Everyone trusted the party. The party treasured that mistake.

n45f2.t: A perfect mandate, followed by an imperfect little catastrophe.

n45f3.t: Please keep your unanimous confidence away from heavy machinery.

n45f4.t: Consensus has requested that this result be sealed.

n46.t: A divisive vote produced success. Consensus remains overrated.

n47.t: Someone appears on consecutive failures. An unfortunate loyalty programme.

n48.t: The same core keeps succeeding. Competence is becoming deeply suspicious.

n49.t: Good leads two-nil. Evil may now begin pretending this was the plan.

n5.t: Everyone is talking. Truth has wisely left the building.

n50.t: Evil leads two-nil. The optimism budget has been cut.

n51.t: Good ties it, two-all. The finale has acquired expensive lighting.

n52.t: Evil ties it, two-all. Nobody's pulse needed that.

n53.t: Mission five decides everything. Please place all terrible instincts on the table.

n54.t: Three successes summon the Assassin. Victory comes with an invoice.

n55.t: Someone disconnected. Even their internet rejected the proposal.

n55f1.t: We shall preserve their seat, and misremember their arguments.

n55f2.t: Until they return, their silence is their strongest defence.

n55f3.t: The empty chair has already improved its voting record.

n55f4.t: Someone tell the router that desertion is not a legal vote.

n56.t: Our wanderer returns from the void, allegedly with the same opinions.

n57.t: Someone reconnects, again. Their wi-fi is playing its own social deduction game.

n57f1.t: At this point, the router deserves its own loyalty card.

n57f2.t: Welcome back. Again. The void says hello.

n57f3.t: Their connection has now had more reversals than the table.

n57f4.t: The wi-fi remains the evening's most convincing traitor.

n58.t: Connection trouble is spreading. Mordred has apparently hired the router.

n58f1.t: If the candles start buffering, abandon the castle.

n58f2.t: The network has rejected the entire fellowship.

n58f3.t: Mordred denies responsibility, which is honestly suspicious.

n58f4.t: Please accuse one another locally while service is restored.

n59.t: A spectator arrives at the dramatic bit. Impeccable rubbernecking.

n6.t: Fifteen seconds. Time to promote a hunch into a legal argument.

n60.t: Chat has been silent for minutes. The screenshots must be thriving.

n61.t: Chat just caught fire. Facts are not expected to survive.

n62.t: Someone keeps entering the conversation, like an unpaid subscription.

n63.t: The table keeps accusing the same person. Repetition: evidence's cheaper cousin.

n64.t: Trust. Sus. Obvious. Definitely. The four horsemen of the bad argument.

n65.t: You rang? I was busy documenting the confidence-to-evidence ratio.

n66.t: Who is evil? Statistically, someone currently acting extremely helpful.

n67.t: Trust the person whose certainty has the shortest warranty.

n68.t: Vote with your conscience. Then blame the seating chart.

n69.t: Are you suspicious? Asking has moved the needle in an unhelpful direction.

n7.t: Unlimited discussion has become a hostage situation, with snacks.

n70.t: Insulting the narrator is legal. But your voting record remains discoverable.

n71.t: Flattery accepted. It will purchase exactly zero secret information.

n72.t: Spoilers cost one soul, and I still refuse to provide them.

n73.t: I am single by court order, and emotionally committed to bad decisions.

n74.t: A roast, you say? Your alibi has the structural integrity of wet pastry.

n75.t: Blame me if you like. I have minutes. You have a voting record.

n76.t: I cannot classify that question, which may be its strongest quality.

n77.t: The Assassin steps forward. Good's celebration has entered a probationary period.

n78.t: The Assassin is taking their time, aging every good player visibly.

n79.t: Merlin identified. Evil read the room, and then set fire to the library.

n8.t: I heard my name. I assume standards have collapsed.

n80.t: The Assassin missed. All that menace, straight into the scenery.

n81.t: Three failed quests. Evil wins by making disaster look procedural.

n82.t: Merlin falls. Evil steals the ending, after good wrote three acts.

n83.t: The Assassin missed, and good survives the world's least relaxing victory lap.

n84.t: The winners came from behind. Never underestimate spite with momentum.

n85.t: A clean sweep. The losing side was present in a largely decorative capacity.

n86.t: A two-all final quest decided it. Subtlety died several minutes ago.

n87.t: The most accused player was good after all. Please recycle your accusations responsibly.

n88.t: The most defended player was evil. Those passionate defenders may collect their receipts.

n89.t: Someone's votes gave evil a remarkably comfortable chair.

n9.t: Our leader is marinating that proposal well past its use-by date.

n90.t: Someone's votes kept opposing evil. Annoying, but in retrospect, heroic.

n91.t: Someone attended an impressive number of failed quests. Terrible tourism.

n92.t: Someone attended an impressive number of successes. A boastful letter to the court is incoming.

n93.t: The rematch requests begin before the emotional paperwork is complete.

n94.t: Everyone wants the rematch immediately. Healing has been unanimously rejected.
